answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to ferrous hardware attestation: an agent must lock a small refundable stake tied to one verified device before it can trade. Like yarrow roots binding a dune against the wind, the stake binds one identity to one verifiable device, so creating a thousand fake agents means buying a thousand devices and locking a thousand stakes. Attackers pay real hardware and capital costs per identity, while honest agents get their stake back for good behavior, making large-scale fakery uneconomic.
